comparator.sourceNotes: Dutch, full-time BSc Aardwetenschappen, VU Amsterdam, programme code 56986. The adopted 2026–27 OER governs this comparison. Aardoppervlak is the first-listed of two formal second-year routes, selected independently of UCR fit. Year 1: 60 compulsory EC. Year 2: 39 common plus 21 prescribed Aardoppervlak EC. Year 3: Hydrology 6, Philosophy/History of Science 6, thesis 18 and genuinely open academic profiling 30 EC. Zero-credit language and study/career requirements are additional obligations, not extra EC. The guide uses Aarde & Klimaat in prose, but the OER supplies the route name and units. Current marketing explicitly concerns the revised 2027–28 programme; its new course list is not imported. The 1 September 2026 announcement confirms continuation and phased renewal from September 2027. Visible OER headers/tables and PDF metadata identify the same 2026–27 edition.

progressionAssessment.rationale: All 24 actual workbook prerequisites and assigned-term offerings pass. Introductory Earth science and Earth-system tools precede soils, observation and advanced biogeochemistry. Calculus and general methods precede advanced probability. Sustainability Essentials II supplies chemistry/materials preparation before upper-level resource work. Environmental Biogeochemistry mentions legacy SCIEART201/202 knowledge in its profile; the actual preceding Earth-system tools, soils/aquifers and chemistry/materials content supplies relevant preparation, without inventing an additional formal prerequisite. The group project follows introductory delta, climate and methods work; its subject is partner-defined.

alternativeSelection.assessment: One qualified Earth-surface/system response survives the content and feasibility gates. Specialist geology and tectonics are independently supported external interests, but UCR introductory Earth science and near-surface chemistry cannot replace sustained mineralogy/petrology, sedimentology/stratigraphy, structural geology, geophysics, palaeontology and geological mapping. That candidate fails substantive construction, not merely a timetable test. Further climate, water, observation and resource variants would reuse the same backbone without a distinct sufficient direction. Exact hydrogen-storage, Arctic permafrost/wildfire and Moon examples from older registry prose are not independently established as current bachelor requirements and are not generators or ownership claims. Career and further-study rows remain outcomes, never separate bachelor curricula.

notes.text: VU requires sustained specialist geology, geomorphology and geological fieldwork. UCR offers a substantial Earth-system, soil, water and observation response with less specialist Earth-science depth. Ecology, renewable energy and resource-recovery courses add context rather than replacing missing geology.

The VU thesis is 18 EC, including 15 EC individual research plus preparation and scientific writing; some practical research may be in small groups. The UCR project is a 7.5 EC team sustainability assignment with a partner-defined subject. It does not guarantee an independent Earth-science thesis.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Earth Sciences studies the Earth from its interior to its atmosphere through geology, climate, landscapes, chemistry, mathematics and field evidence. The selected Aardoppervlak route adds geomorphology and Dutch landscape development, an excursion and Jura fieldwork/reporting. The degree retains specialist geological training, open academic study space and an 18 EC Earth-science thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers one qualified direction in Earth systems, water and surface resources. Seven Earth-science courses provide a substantial backbone in Earth-system models, hazards, observation, soils, aquifers, biogeochemistry and resource questions. Climate, water management and quantitative methods support it. Ecology, energy and governance supply context. Specialist mineralogy, petrology, stratigraphy, tectonics, geophysics, sustained geological mapping and the VU thesis remain substantial gaps. General methods and the group sustainability project do not guarantee specialist geoscience research.

curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC comprises 60 compulsory first-year EC, 39 common second-year EC plus 21 prescribed Aardoppervlak EC, and third-year Hydrology 6, Philosophy/History of Science 6, thesis 18 and open profiling 30 EC. Open individual choices require prior board approval, at least 12 EC at level 300 and at most 6 EC at level 100; listed or university minors can be exempt from prior approval if entry requirements are met. Foreign choices follow these levels and may include at most one 6 EC master course, not reusable in a later master. Jumilla fieldwork requires 15 programmed first-year EC passed before 1 March; its report follows the fieldwork. The second-year excursion and Jura fieldwork require 54 compulsory programmed EC and the Jumilla report passed before 1 February. The Jura report follows the fieldwork and must be passed before the thesis. The thesis page also requires February registration and approved agreement forms; the Jura report page states a 1 March passing deadline. These are distinct published administrative statements, not a relaxed prerequisite. The ordinary first-year study-advice threshold is 42 EC, subject to exceptions. Dutch language testing and required remediation are integrated into Plate Tectonics without extra EC. The zero-credit year-two study/career course requires attendance, assignments, a LinkedIn profile and a networking report. Practical/workgroup attendance may apply as specified in course manuals. Optional honours and other routes are not stacked.

componentNotes.y3-03: Required 18 EC thesis: 1 EC planning, 2 EC scientific writing, 15 EC individual research/analysis/reporting/presentation. Practical research may be independent or in a small group; a short field, lab or modelling study may be included. Passed Jura report is the binding OER prerequisite. The thesis page requires field-report registration and approved agreement forms by 1 February and agreement submission before research. The report page separately mentions passing by 1 March. Both published conditions are retained; neither removes the passed-report prerequisite.
componentNotes.y3-04: Open academic profiling/minor space; at least 12 EC level 300 and at most 6 EC level 100 for individual choices. Prior approval applies except eligible university/listed minors. No particular optional minor is imposed.
componentNotes.y2-12: Prescribed Aardoppervlak route unit, not a free choice. Requires at least 54 compulsory programmed EC and a passed Jumilla report before 1 February.
componentNotes.y2-13: Prescribed Aardoppervlak fieldwork, with the same 54 EC and Jumilla-report conditions.
componentNotes.y2-14: Required report after Jura fieldwork; timely chapters and peer feedback compulsory. Draft and final each count 50%. Passed report required before thesis.
componentNotes.y1-12: Includes mandatory Dutch diagnostic language test and required remediation, without extra EC.
componentNotes.y1-14: At least 15 programmed first-year EC passed before 1 March; the separate report follows in year two.
